title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: S&P 500 (7,818.93) and Nasdaq (27,599.79) closed at fresh records Tuesday, +0.6% and +0.5%; Dow added 253 points (+0.5%) to 51,521.28.
Markets: 10-year Treasury yield eased to ~5.27% after touching its highest level since 2002 on Monday; Treasury auctions $39B in 10-year notes Wednesday.
Markets: Brent crude ticked up 0.3% to $100.58/bbl, still near the $100 threshold on Strait of Hormuz tanker-attack risk; French 10-year yields hover near 5% on fiscal worries.
Companies: Chip stocks mixed — Seagate -9% and Western Digital -7% on acquisition/bidding-contest reports, while Marvell jumped ~6% after an investor-day revenue target.
Companies: Smart-ring maker Oura shelved its IPO after failing to find buyers at its target price, citing jittery markets despite indices near record highs.
Macro/Policy: FOMC meeting minutes due Wednesday after the Fed's latest quarter-point cut, with officials split on whether policy remains restrictive.
Macro/Policy: US trade deficit narrowed ~24% in August to $59.6B as tariffs curbed imports; EU continues weighing tougher measures against Chinese imports and critical-mineral dependence.
